items.note: Meta-analysis of 28 studies (8,214 participants in total) pooling GenAI vs human creativity (g = -0.05), humans with vs without GenAI (g = 0.27), and idea diversity with GenAI (g = -0.86); arXiv v1 only, abstract read from the arXiv landing page; useful as a source list of primary experiments.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref empty; ScienceDirect 403); title suggests a study of human-GenAI collaboration at different creative phases with novelty and usefulness outcomes, so it is kept as a possible experiment for full-text check.

Self-described selective narrative review (2018-2026) of LLMs as tools, models, and partners in creativity research using the GCA framework; reports a range of g from independent AI-vs-human comparisons but is not systematic.
Compares 151 human participants with GPT-4 on the Alternative Uses, Consequences, and Divergent Associations tasks; no participant receives AI help; AI scores higher on originality and elaboration.

Screenplays produced under human-only, minimal-intervention AI, and iterative human-AI collaboration conditions are rated blind by industry experts; the abstract does not say how many writers took part or whether conditions were assigned, so the full text must show whether people were assigned to AI conditions (it may be closer to an AI-vs-human output comparison).

Scoping review of human-AI co-creativity in storytelling (LNCS chapter); abstract not reachable (Semantic Scholar elided by publisher, Crossref empty, OpenAlex timed out, Springer redirect to login); next stage should check whether its search is systematic or it is a narrative review (then out).

95 participants randomized to LLM creativity instruction, human instruction, or no-intervention control; Alternative Uses Task fluency, originality, and flexibility scored at acquisition and transfer (transfer likely after_ai), plus fNIRS and self-reports; AI here is an instructor, not a production aid.

Two experiments in which creators make images with a text-to-image tool while expecting AI-use disclosure to lay audiences, experts, or not; audiences rate novelty, appeal, and quality; all creators use AI, so conditions differ in anticipated disclosure rather than AI access, and the next stage should judge whether this counts as an AI-configuration contrast.

Within-subjects electronic brainstorming with groups without GenAI, groups with GenAI, and individuals with GenAI (N = 24); idea counts, quality, originality, elaboration, and flexibility scored; below the 50-participant threshold and order randomization not stated.

164 university students assigned to AI use or no AI for a future-idea task, then randomly branched in a revision round into continued use, discontinuation, adoption, or continued non-use; ideas scored on a four-dimension creativity rubric; abstract read from the KACE journal page (Korean journal), and the round-1 assignment method should be confirmed in the full text.
